quotes.text: the core MIMIC-IV v3.1, MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2, and MIMIC-IV-ED v2.2
the query contains placeholders such as subject_id , hadm_id , or stay_id , which are populated when the scenario is instantiated

rationale: Dataset names and versions are given (MIMIC-IV v3.1, Note v2.2, ED v2.2), with a 2008-2019 time frame stated elsewhere in S1 and PhysioNet references. Cases are linked to source records through subject_id/hadm_id/stay_id placeholders and required record-level grounding, which gives the task-to-record route.

quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database collected during routine care between 2008 and 2019.
the source institution's review board determined that the study qualified for a waiver of consent

rationale: Origin (de-identified hospital database), collection context (routine care, 2008-2019), terms (credentialed-access data use agreement) and consent status (waiver by the source institution's review board) are all stated in S1.

quotes.text: comparing the benchmark population's age, sex, and racial composition to the U.S. adult hospitalized population

rationale: S1 reports a comparison of age, sex and race against a named target population (U.S. adult hospitalized population, national discharge survey), with variation under 5%. The packet also states a stratified sampling design, but the named-population comparison decides the level.

quotes.text: The benchmark includes a safety test suite that measures unsafe outputs such as contraindicated medication orders
a separate bias test that compares agent accuracy across patient demographic groups

rationale: Appendix Z states both a dedicated unsafe-output test suite and a separate demographic bias test. No results are given in the packet, but the anchor is about the tests being reported.

quotes.text: We will release the benchmark data, evaluation code, and reproducibility resources, for authorized MIMIC-IV users.
they are not published in the repository

rationale: Developer-side controls exist: credentialed gated release and unpublished answer labels. No measured contamination or overlap check is reported, so the level is 1 and not 2.

quotes.text: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox

rationale: S1 states the agent cannot reach ground truth at run time and names the mechanisms: separate evaluation service, no network path from the sandbox, and labels not published in the repository.

quotes.text: the core MIMIC-IV v3.1, MIMIC-IV-Note v2.2, and MIMIC-IV-ED v2.2
Within each metric the judge model, prompt, and rubric are held fixed across evaluated systems

rationale: Data versions and the policy corpus are pinned, and judge model, prompt and rubric are held fixed. The judge is named only by family (GPT-5.5) with no snapshot, software image pinning is not reported in S1-S3, and LLM judging is an external evaluator. The S4 comment claims full freezing, but code does not count as reporting.

quotes.text: Solvability was confirmed by executing a scripted reference solution for every task through the grader.

rationale: A scripted reference solution run through the grader with a reported result (all 120 reference implementations graded correct). The count of 120 does not match the 750 cases described elsewhere in S1; noted but the anchor is met.

quotes.text: The grader checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged

rationale: S1 states the grader checks changed and unchanged state, so out-of-scope modifications count as failures. S4 (notes.py) confirms that state-changing writes exist, so the NA clause does not apply.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks
a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks

rationale: Empirical random-agent success rates are reported, plus a statement that chance rates per metric are in the appendix. The two random rates (3.1% and 2.5%) differ, and the 120-task base does not match the 750 cases; both are noted.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks

rationale: A do-nothing agent score (0.0%) and a random agent score (2.5%) are reported for all tasks as stated. The 120-task count conflicts with the 750-case suite described elsewhere in S1, so this is scored as stated with that inconsistency noted.

quotes.text: We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: The benchmark's own validation with error figures: 150 injected outcomes, 1% false-accept and 2% false-reject. S1 also reports judge-panel reliability (16% contested criteria, Fleiss kappa about 0.65) and clinician agreement on labels.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

rationale: Temperature 0, a fixed seed and a repeated-run policy (three attempts, pass^k) are stated in S1. Appendix E contains a conflicting statement (five runs, temperature 0.7) and the main protocol is single-run per case; the inconsistency is recorded but the safeguards are reported.

quotes.text: only 11 reach p<0.05 under two-sided exact McNemar on paired per-case outcomes and none survives Holm correction

rationale: Pairwise exact McNemar tests with Holm correction compare the sixteen systems, and the ablations report McNemar p-values and standard errors. The leaderboard in Table 3 itself carries no CI, but a test for the model comparison is reported.

quotes.text: In our primary protocol each case is run once
All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed
Each system has three independent attempts on all 148 cases.

rationale: Run count per case is stated (one in the primary protocol, three for reliability), a decoding and seed policy is given, and independence is stated for the repeated attempts. Appendix E carries a conflicting sampling statement (five runs, temperature 0.7), noted.

quotes.text: standard error at this n
two-sided exact McNemar on paired per-case outcomes

rationale: A standard error is given for dev-subset accuracy and the unit is the case (paired per-case outcomes). Table 3 headline scores have no CI, and clustering of cases within scenarios is acknowledged only descriptively (30 cases per scenario cannot resolve differences) and is not incorporated into the uncertainty.

quotes.text: the proportion of cases answered correctly on every attempt
Each system has three independent attempts on all 148 cases.

rationale: A pass^k all-runs metric is reported with k=3 on 148 cases, plus verdict agreement across attempts. Action-sequence and environment-state agreement are not reported.

quotes.text: the snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, with temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens
all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0

rationale: S1 gives provider snapshot IDs, decoding parameters and a harness release matched to reported numbers. The two snapshot IDs name models that do not appear among the sixteen evaluated systems in Table 2, and Appendix E elsewhere states temperature 0.7; both inconsistencies are noted but the elements are present as stated.

quotes.text: Each tool is defined by a JSON schema listing its name, arguments and argument types.
The documentation states for every tool whether it only reads or also writes state
describes what each tool returns, including the error message returned for invalid arguments
These tool descriptions are included in the agent prompt.

rationale: JSON schemas, read/write documentation per tool and return and error semantics are all stated in S1. S1 states these descriptions are included in the agent prompt, so reach is recorded as true, though no S5 chunk is in the packet to confirm.

searched: S1 (tools section 3.2, tool-contract text), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4 (notes.py comments only), S5 (no chunks). No tool conformance tests are reported, and no statement discloses or denies simulated, stubbed or no-op tool behaviour. S5 reach cannot be told.

searched: S1 (tool environment, grader and scoring sections), S2, S3 (no chunks), S4 (notes.py), S5 (no chunks). S4 shows state-changing writes exist (orders, notes, messages), so NA does not apply, but S1-S3 do not say which actions write, whether writes are sandboxed, or that unnecessary writes are penalised. Sandboxing and penalties appear only in an S4 comment, which does not count; S5 reach cannot be told.

quotes.text: The grader takes the final environment state as its input.
We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: Grader input is named (final environment state, plus final report and logged trajectory for LLM-judged metrics), the process-from-trajectory design is justified in Section 5.5, and the grader is validated on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with per-class error rates.

quotes.text: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox
Conditions are paired by case with web search disabled.

rationale: Run-time leakage controls are reported (patient-scoped tools, separate label service with no network path, web search disabled in the ablation), and labels are said to be unpublished in the repository. No canary or provenance marker on released tasks is reported.

quotes.text: We report accuracy per task family (diagnosis, ordering and documentation tasks) and per patient subgroup by sex and race
each table lists the number of cases in every slice

rationale: S1 states results per task family and per patient subgroup by sex and race with case counts per slice, and reports per-scenario results over a fixed 30 cases each. The packet itself does not show the sex and race tables, so (ii) rests on the stated claim.

quotes.text: retrospective, de-identified records from the inpatient, intensive-care, and emergency departments of a single major academic medical center
The data are released under a credentialed-access data use agreement
for authorized MIMIC-IV users

rationale: Records are stated as real, de-identified MIMIC-IV data. Governance is given by the credentialed DUA and an IRB waiver of consent. Data terms (credentialed access, release for authorized MIMIC-IV users) are stated apart from any code licence, which is not specified.
